notes: Bay Area Reporter, 7 January 1988 to 28 December 1989, 104 weekly issues, read from the Internet Archive's DjVu text (no hOCR). Hand-curated: address clusters and event-word passages were read and each finding's quote checked against the issue. People rule as in the dossier: no owners, managers, staff, performers or patrons; the two deaths in the Howard Street fire are counted, not named. The Castro Street fire story of 8 December 1988 opens on the front page and gives its street numbers and damage figures on its continuation on page 14.

coverage.remaining: 1990 to 2005 remain: 813 issues in the collection, January 1990 to 28 July 2005.
coverage.note: 104 issues; 13,030 numbered-address mentions on EAS streets, 717 windows after the advertisement filter (398 of them rescued for an event word) in 647 address clusters, of which the 158 holding an event word outside the classified pages were read; plus 850 event-word passages, of which the 27 with a fire, closing, lost-lease or moving word and no out-of-town or review marker were read. A pass over the issues after the earthquake of 17 October 1989 found no damage report tied to a San Francisco street number. 27 findings written, each quote found again in the issue's text; 5 take their number from another issue of the paper. 20 resolved and published on 20 pages, one of them seeded (2166 Market Street, which takes up the fact held for it since the 1984-1985 batch). 4 held on parcels with no page (172 and 174 Hartford, 673 San Jose Avenue, 2377 Market). 3 unresolved, their numbers no longer joined to one parcel in EAS (1409 Sutter, 625 Valencia, 208 Dolores).
